db_evidence.notes: episodes:30sec:002475 (74250-74280) textually captions the defeat banner as '妖王·翠云金睳兽' (Cuiyun/green-cloud Golden-Eyed Beast) rather than the reference's '碧水金睳兽' (Bishui/blue-water Golden-Eyed Beast) — a plausible OCR/caption misread of near-identical boss names, so pure text search on this row alone would produce a slightly wrong name. Rollouts 1 and 3 both resolved this correctly by running clip_qa directly on the 74190-74280s interval, which visually read the on-screen text as '碧水金睳兽', matching the reference. The subsequent weapon-forging/equipment screens at 74400-74541s (entity 'weapon: 白枪 (white spear)' with first_seen_s 74400) corroborate that this is the point after which the spear stops being used. All the needed evidence (episodes captions, an entities row for the spear, and clip_qa-verifiable frames) is present in the DB and was retrievable with straightforward run_sql/semantic_search over the full 0-85000s timeline plus one clip_qa call.

root_causes: Three rollouts (0, 2, 4) stopped their temporal search too early: each found a boss fight where the player visibly used the spear, treated an intermediate/looks-final weapon change as THE last switch, and submitted without continuing the search to the true end of the video (~74,000-85,000s) to rule out later spear usage.

The task requires an exhaustive last-occurrence search across the entire ~85,000s timeline, but semantic_search top-k results for 'chubai spear' cluster around several boss fights (55,000s, 72,000s, 74,000s) with similar scores, so an agent that clip_qa-confirms the first plausible-looking one and stops will land on a wrong, earlier answer.

Rollouts 1 and 3 succeeded because they combined broad run_sql LIKE-scans across the full timeline (not just top semantic_search hits) with an explicit run_sql/entities lookup narrowing to the true last-seen window (~74,000-74,500s), then used a single confirmatory clip_qa there.

A caption-level OCR/name confusion exists in the episodes table ('翠云' vs '碧水' Golden-Eyed Beast) but did not cause any of the observed failures, since successful rollouts read the correct name from clip_qa rather than trusting the episodes caption text alone.
what_worked: Running a full-timeline run_sql LIKE scan for 'chubai'/'chu bai'/'spear' (and Chinese variants like '白枪') across multiple tables to avoid relying only on top-k semantic_search hits
Querying the entities table for a 'weapon: white spear' row and using its first_seen_s/last_seen_s as a concrete anchor for the true last-usage window
Narrowing to the 72,000-85,000s range specifically (not stopping at intermediate weapon-switch events around 55,000-57,500s) before committing to a clip_qa confirmation
Using clip_qa as the final confirmation step on a specific ~60-90s window rather than trusting the episodes table's free-text caption alone, which correctly resolved the boss-name OCR ambiguity
transferable_lessons: For 'last occurrence before X stops happening' questions, do not stop at the first weapon-switch/behavior-change event that looks plausible — explicitly continue the search through the end of the timeline to rule out a later re-occurrence of the target behavior.

Cross-check any 'switch away from weapon' event found mid-timeline against later time ranges; an early switch may be temporary (switched back later), so only a switch with no subsequent target-weapon usage counts as final.

When multiple semantic_search hits for the same query cluster at different times with similar scores, treat that as a signal of multiple candidate occurrences requiring disambiguation by time order, not evidence that the first result found is correct.
Prefer entities-table first_seen_s/last_seen_s lookups (when a table row exists for the object of interest) as a cheap way to bound the true last-usage window before spending clip_qa calls.

Trust clip_qa's visual read of on-screen boss/item names over the episodes/visual_clips caption text when they conflict, since captions can have OCR-like name confusions between visually similar strings (e.g. '翠云' vs '碧水').
open_questions: Whether the episodes caption's '翠云金睳兽' vs reference's '碧水金睳兽' reflects an actual OCR error in the captioning pipeline or two visually near-identical bosses with different names in the game; not fully resolved without inspecting the raw frame pixels directly.
